title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of the preparatory notes for Grothendieck's 1976 IHÉS lecture on the de Rham complex with divided powers. The surrounding pages build a simplicial and cosimplicial apparatus based on the standard simplices Δ^n. The page is photographed upside down. The previous page gives the key model.

The exterior-algebra model of a simplex:
- The normalized cochains of Δ^n are C^p_{[n]} = Λ^{p+1}(k^{Δ^n}), with k^{Δ^n} = k^{n+1}. A (p+1)-subset of {0,…,n} is a p-face, giving a basis element e_{i_0}∧…∧e_{i_p}.
- The coboundary is wedge product with T_n = Σ e_i.
- Dually, the chains C^{[n]}_p = Λ^{p+1} k^{n+1} have boundary given by interior product with the augmentation form (T_n viewed as a linear form). This is the 'produit intérieur par T_n' on this page.
- As n varies, n ↦ C^·_{[n]} is a simplicial cochain complex and n ↦ C^{[n]}_· is a cosimplicial chain complex. They are k-dual to each other: (C^*)^∨ = C_* = k[Δ^n_*].

What this page does:
- It considers the functors L^· ↦ Hom(X^·, L^·) and, for a complex X, the object n ↦ Hom_·(C^{[n]}_·, X^·), i.e. Hom_·(C^*_·, X^·). This is the simplicial module attached to X by mapping out of the chains of the standard simplices: Kan's form of the Dold–Kan functor, K(X)_n = Hom(N k[Δ^n], X).
- The commutative square sends C^·_n → X^· down to C^·_{n-1} → X^·_{n-1} via d and the interior product by T_n. It checks that the differential of X matches the simplicial structure. The face/degeneracy pairs K^{n-1} ⇄ K^n labelled (∂*, s*) record these structure maps.
- The identities Hom(X_·, C^·_·) = X^∨ express that mapping into the simplicial cochain object recovers the dual. Since Δ^n is contractible, C^·(Δ^n) is acyclic with H^0 = k; the bracketed definitions of C as 'K si … ; 0 si …' appear to be normalized versus non-normalized variants concentrated in a single degree.
- The crossed-out lines try Hom(X^·, C^·_n) in the other variance and abandon it.

Purpose: to set up the comparison between complexes and (co)simplicial modules needed to define functors F_{Δ^n_*} and their multiplicative structure. The next page continues with K(M_*) → F(M_*) ⇉ F'(M_*), with tensor products via the diagonal M → M⊗M, and with Λ^2 Ψ_{[n]}. That leads toward the simplicial divided-power de Rham algebra.
errors: No mathematical errors identifiable. The notation is fluid: dot versus star for normalized versus non-normalized, and upper versus lower indices are used inconsistently. Some identities (e.g. Hom(X_·, C^·_*) = X^∨) are only correct up to the choice of normalization and degree conventions, which are not fixed on the page.
The definitions in the lower-right corner of the image (C = 'K si … , 0 si …') are incomplete. The conditions are not legible or not written.

ideas.what: Cochains/chains of Δ^n as exterior powers Λ^{p+1} k^{n+1}, with differential given by wedge with, or interior product by, T_n = Σ e_i
ideas.modern_name: Koszul/exterior-algebra model of simplicial (co)chains of the standard simplex
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Eilenberg–Mac Lane era; standard in Koszul complex treatments)

ideas.what: Simplicial module n ↦ Hom(C_*(Δ^n), X) attached to a complex X; duality between the cosimplicial chain complex and the simplicial cochain complex
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan correspondence (Kan's description via the cosimplicial complex N k[Δ^•])

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping: the exterior-algebra model of simplex (co)chains and a Kan-style Dold–Kan functor, written as preparation for the divided-power de Rham construction. Nothing new on this page itself.
transcription_corrections: The page is photographed upside down; reading order runs from the bottom-right of the image upward.
The handwritten page number in the corner is '342' (archive sequence 340).
In the commutative square, the vertical arrow labelled 'd' joins the X-terms. The left vertical arrow is annotated 'produit intérieur par T_n', and the target is C^·_{n-1} → X^·_{n-1}.
The doubled arrows K^{n-1} ⇇ K^n and K^{n-1} ⇄ K^n carry the labels ∂* and s* (faces and degeneracies), with extra arrowheads drawn, indicating several face maps.
